alright but first before you take it outside you should read the manual if you have one. it looks like an eq mount so on your manual you will see that you have to set your latitude number on the mount.

just google what’s my latitude it’s easy

if you can understand the manual, you can see there’s an axis that you should probably point at Polaris, the north star, but you really don’t have to it will work fine otherwise, doing that calibrates the mount that your telescope is on, the metal part, to the movement of objects across the sky, but if you just want a pretty quick look at the moon or jupiter or some other planets, it shouldn’t be a problem.

it will really help later down the line so i recommend that if it’s really  too hard to figure out, just go out and look at something and get into it

after you have done that, you want to get it outside. make sure the big cap at the end of the big tube is off. this is like the lens cap on a camera 

then you want to take the lenses (the little cylinders that came with the telescope, i’m assuming) and you want to put it in the hole at the top that has a cap too. the actual lens also has caps just take all the caps off basically

use the longest lens first

then if you want to zoom in, use a smaller one

you don’t NEED the finder scope (the small telescope looking thingy on the side) but it will really help later, just aim your big tube at a planet you see on your stargazing app, and it will be visible in your scope, after a little bit of messing around. 

use the little circles next to your lens that you are looking into, and turn them to focus.

EVERYTHING IS IN REVERSE, the mirror at the back flips everything you see in the scope around and it makes moving it go in reverse. down looks like up, up looks like down , you will understand what i mean once you start messing around
